newsitem.title: UK: Allied Domecq expects better second half.
newsitem.headline: Allied Domecq expects better second half.

text.p: British drinks-to-pubs group Allied Domecq expects its performance in the second half of the year to benefit from higher spirits shipments to the United States and more investement in its pubs, chairman Sir Christopher Hogg said on Tuesday.
His remarks were attached to the group's first half financial results which showed a three percent increase in pre-tax profits to 317 milion pounds before the impact of adverse currency movements.

Brokers estimates ranged from 304 to 325 million pounds ($527 million). The dividend was maintained at 9.44 pence per share rather than a slight increase as many had anticipated. For the year as a whole, Hogg said, there would be an estimated adverse impact from currency translation of about 28 million pounds.
"The challenge for Allied now is to demonstrate that it can deliver improving financial performance - particularly in the spirits business where market conditions remain testing," said Hogg.

Spirits and wine turnover was up one percent but trading profits were down two percent at 239 million pounds. Sales in Europe were down three percent and in America one percent lower. In Europe, volume increases in Spain and Germany were offset by declines in volume in Britain, Greece and Italy.

In Britain, Teacher's whisky lost volume in the face of tougher pricing by competitors but sales of Courvoisier brandy improved. The company concentrates its marketing effort on four core brands -- Ballantine's, Beefeater, Kahlua and Sauza.

Trading profit from the group's retailing division fell one percent to 105 million pounds with growth in its managed pubs being offset by lower profits from off-licence chain Victoria Wine. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
